correctness.rationale: The generator has exact positive-flip rate δ b_v(S)/2 and negative-flip rate (1−δ/2) times the exposed negative neighbor fraction. On a connected induced dissenting component all nonempty proper subsets have positive loss rate at δ=0, making the transient generator invertible. Backward induction gives the stated coefficients; geometric excursion renewal yields an exponential waiting limit with explicit positive rate. Independent components give a maximum of independent exponentials. Expectations converge by bounded second moments, not merely finite numerical checks. The exact-rational script independently agrees with asymptotic prefactors and a four-node countercontrast.

originality.rationale: Finite-graph metastable consensus exponent, exact positive recursive coefficients and limiting maximum-of-exponentials distribution were compared by scientific implication with full accessible 2023 primary models, published classical partisan-voter literature, indexed mathematical research summaries, and the available 2025 closely related abstract. The 2023 studies supply the copying mechanism, mean-field stability and finite mean-field fixation models, but do not establish the arbitrary finite-graph induced-component exponent, recursion, or limiting distribution. General finite-chain perturbation theory can underpin the proof, so an unindexed direct specialization remains a genuine residual priority risk, not a certified global novelty statement.

value.rationale: The precise induced-component invariant solves a motivated opinion-dynamics question: how an almost uncompromising dissenting population can still eventually reach consensus under a nonempty committed majority. Two equal-order graphs with one zealot and three dissidents have sharply different mean-time divergence exponents (1 versus 3). The theorem gives all-graph exponents, explicit computable rational prefactors and a distributional limiting law; these are not merely normalization or tiny finite sample improvements.
